previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman was admitted for evaluation of progressive weakness and recurrent falls, occurring in the context of poor oral intake and overuse of diuretics. She presented with lightheadedness, exertional chest pain, and dehydration. Initial labs revealed acute kidney injury, hyponatremia, elevated lactate, and leukocytosis, all attributed to hypovolemia from excessive diuresis. An ECG showed deep T-wave inversions and a mildly elevated troponin, consistent with a Type II NSTEMI secondary to supply-demand imbalance. Imaging showed no acute intracranial or intra-abdominal processes, a stable pancreatic cyst, and no fractures. She was rehydrated with IV fluids, her torsemide dose was reduced, and metolazone was discontinued. Aspirin was resumed after hematologic consultation. Her symptoms improved, renal function normalized, and she was discharged to extended care with stable vital signs, improved strength, and a plan for outpatient follow-up.

INDICATION:  History: ___ w PMH of CAD, aortic dissection w repair, HTN
presents to the ED s/p fall.  // Does she have any pulmonary infiltrates?

TECHNIQUE:  Chest:  Frontal and Lateral

COMPARISON:  ___

FINDINGS: 

Patient is status post median sternotomy.  Bibasilar opacities persist which
may be due to atelectasis and scarring.  No definite new focal consolidation
is seen although would be difficult to exclude on the left.  No pleural
effusion or pneumothorax is seen.  The cardiac and mediastinal silhouettes are
stable.  Multiple old right-sided rib deformities are again seen.

IMPRESSION: 

Similar appearance of the chest compared ___ without definite new
focal consolidation, although one would be difficult to exclude at the left
lung base.

EXAMINATION:  CT HEAD W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION:  ___ female with past medical history of coronary artery
disease, non ST elevation myocardial infarct, aortic dissection status post
repair and hypertension presents the ED via ambulance status post mechanical
fall with occipital head laceration.  Evaluate for intracranial bleed.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial images of the brain were obtained without
contrast. Coronal and sagittal reformations as well as bone algorithm
reconstructions were provided and reviewed.

DOSE:  Total DLP (Head) = 803 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  CT head from ___ and ___.

FINDINGS: 

There is no evidence of acute vascular territorial infarction, hemorrhage,
edema, or mass.  There is prominence of the ventricles and sulci suggestive of
involutional changes.  Incidental note is made of ___ cisterna magna. 
Periventricular white matter hypodensities may reflect chronic small vessel
ischemic disease

There is no evidence of acute fracture.  The visualized portion of the
paranasal sinuses, mastoid air cells, and middle ear cavities are clear.  The
patient is status post bilateral lens replacement.

IMPRESSION: 

No acute intracranial abnormality.

EXAMINATION:  CT C-SPINE W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION:  ___ female status post fall.  Evaluate for fracture.

TECHNIQUE:  Non-contrast helical multidetector CT of the cervical spine was
performed. Soft tissue and bone algorithm images were generated.  Coronal and
sagittal reformations were then constructed.

DOSE:  Total DLP (Body) = 711 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  CT cervical spine from ___ and ___.

FINDINGS: 

Alignment of the cervical spine is unchanged.  No acute fracture or
prevertebral soft tissue swelling is noted.  A screw is again noted through a
prior dens fracture, and there is a similar lucency along the superior and
posterior aspect of this screw.  Fusion of the bilateral C3-C4 facets are
noted.  There is mild narrowing of the spinal canal due to posterior disc
osteophyte complexes at C4-C5, C5-C6 and C6-C7.  There are moderate
degenerative changes including disc height loss, endplate irregularity,
subchondral cyst formation and anterior and posterior osteophytosis, most
pronounced at C5-C6 and C6-C7.  Ill-defined thyroid hypodense nodules are
noted.  The visualized lung apices are grossly clear.

IMPRESSION:


1. No acute fracture or traumatic malalignment.
2. Unchanged appearance of a screw transfixing a chronic type II dens fracture
with lucency along the distal tip of the screw.
